title: Before-Save vs After-Save Record-Triggered Flow
objectives: Choose before-save (fast field updates on the triggering record) versus after-save (actions and related records) from the outcome.
Cite why before-save record-triggered Flow can update that record before it is saved, and is documented as faster than a record-change process.
Use Flow Trigger Explorer and trigger order values to see before-save, after-save, and asynchronous paths on one object.
Refuse before-save when the work is email, related-record DML, or a human approval, and refuse Apex when after-save Flow already fits.
diagnostic_question: A LAB_ Course Attendee needs a status defaulted on the same record, then a related waitlist record updated and an email sent. Before reading, which path is before-save versus after-save, and what evidence would make you reject a validation rule or Apex?
definition: A record-triggered Flow starts when a record is created, updated, or deleted. Before-save (optimize for fast field updates) can make additional updates to that same record before it is saved to the database and is documented as up to 10 times faster than a record-change process. After-save (optimize for actions and related records) runs later in the save order and is the path for related records, emails, and other actions. ([Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger.htm); [Before-Save Record-Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm); [Bulkified Record Processing](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_example_bulkified_processing.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for 'same record, before the database save' versus 'related records and actions after save.' Putting email or Task creation on a before-save path, or writing Apex for a same-record stamp a before-save Flow can do, is a common fail. Order of execution is the deeper map (APEX-009); this lesson is the Flow fork.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an airport. Before-save is passport control: you can still correct the same passport before the traveler is admitted to the country—the record is not yet saved. After-save is the arrivals concierge: the traveler is in the country, so you can book a hotel, text a ride, or create a luggage ticket (related records and actions). Validation is the 'you may not enter' stamp; a formula is the always-visible visa class on the passport; approval is a secondary interview with immigration; Apex is a custom hangar when Flow cannot do the job.
deeper_explanation: Triggered Flows Help: creating or updating a record can trigger a record-triggered flow to make additional updates to that record before it is saved to the database. A record-triggered flow can update a Salesforce record 10 times faster than a record-change process. Configure the record trigger on the Start element. ([Before-Save Record-Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm); [Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger.htm))

After-save is selected when you optimize the flow for Actions and Related Records. Help's bulkification example uses an after-save Opportunity flow to Get Records and create Tasks, and notes that after-save runs later in the order than before-save; details of that order live in Triggers and Order of Execution. ([Bulkified Record Processing](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_example_bulkified_processing.htm))

Flow Trigger Explorer shows record-triggered flows for an object that run when a record is created, updated, or deleted, including before-save, after-save, and asynchronous paths. You can assign a trigger order value from 1 to 2,000 so before-save or after-save flows on the same object run in a predictable sequence. ([Triggered Flows](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger.htm))

AUTO-001 still applies. A validation rule refuses an illegal save; it does not stamp a default. A formula field calculates without a Flow interview. An approval process routes a person. Apex is complementary for CPU-heavy work or Batch Apex volume—not the default for a same-record before-save update. Custom Error is a record-triggered Flow element (Flow Types); do not invent its full behavior here.

Scheduled paths on a record-triggered Flow run part of the flow at a configurable offset after the triggering event. They are not the same as before-save. Needs verification before claiming async governor numbers; Help's bulkification page mentions after-save for follow-up Tasks and higher limits on some asynchronous work—confirm the current article before quoting numbers.

mental_model.analogy: Airport passport control versus the arrivals concierge: before-save still edits the same passport before admission; after-save happens after the traveler is in the country and can create tickets and send messages.
useful_mapping: before-save / fast field updates → correct the same record before the database save
after-save / actions and related records → related DML, email, and other actions after save
validation rule → refused entry (illegal data never saves)
formula field → visa class printed on the passport (always computed)
approval process → a secondary human interview, not a field stamp
Flow Trigger Explorer → the airport's board of all flights (flows) for that object
trigger order 1–2000 → which checkpoint runs first among same-kind flows
where_it_breaks: One Salesforce save can run validation, before-save Flow, after-save Flow, and Apex triggers—more than two airport rooms (APEX-009).
The 10x claim is versus a record-change process, not versus Apex.
Scheduled paths and asynchronous paths are extra rooms, not before-save.
Edition and API version change which elements exist on each path; do not invent a full element allow-list.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Before-save updates the same record before the database save and is documented as faster than a record-change process. After-save is for actions and related records. Validation still blocks illegal data. Apex is complementary, not the default stamp.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I ask whether the change is only fields on the triggering record. If yes, I optimize for fast field updates (before-save). If I need Get Records, create Tasks, send email, or submit approval, I optimize for actions and related records (after-save). I use Flow Trigger Explorer and trigger order 1–2000 when multiple flows share an object. I do not use before-save as a validation rule, and I do not write Apex for a same-record default a before-save Flow can do.

terminology.plain: A flow that starts when a record is created, updated, or deleted.
terminology.precise: Configure the trigger on the Start element. Help lists record-created, updated, deleted, and scheduled paths on record-triggered flows.
terminology.example: Opportunity updated to Closed Won starts an after-save Flow.
terminology.non_example: A screen Flow the user clicks is not record-triggered.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Schedule-triggered Flow: time batch, not a record save.

terminology.plain: The record-triggered path that updates the triggering record before it is saved.
terminology.precise: Help: additional updates to that record before it is saved to the database; up to 10 times faster than a record-change process. In the Start element this is the fast field updates optimization.
terminology.example: Default LAB_ Status__c on the same Course Attendee before insert commits.
terminology.non_example: Sending an email is not before-save work.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Validation rule: refuses the save instead of stamping a field.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent a full element list; confirm in Builder.

terminology.plain: The record-triggered path for actions and related records after the save.
terminology.precise: Optimize the Flow for Actions and Related Records. Help's example creates Tasks after Closed Won and notes after-save runs later than before-save.
terminology.example: Create follow-up LAB_ Tasks and email attendees after save.
terminology.non_example: A formula field is not after-save.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Asynchronous / scheduled path: time-offset, not the immediate after-save path.

terminology.plain: The Start-element optimization that selects the before-save path.
terminology.precise: Tied to updating the triggering record before the database save, not to related-record DML.
terminology.example: Optimize for Fast Field Updates when only LAB_ fields on $Record change.
terminology.non_example: Apex Database.update on related contacts is not this optimization.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Actions and Related Records: the after-save label.
terminology.boundary: UI wording can vary; match the org.

terminology.plain: The view of all record-triggered flows for an object and trigger type.
terminology.precise: Shows flows that run on create, update, or delete, including before-save, after-save, and asynchronous paths, and lets you navigate among them.
terminology.example: Open Explorer on Opportunity to see two before-save and one after-save Flow.
terminology.non_example: Setup → Validation Rules is not Explorer.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Trigger order value: the numeric sequence, not the Explorer itself.
terminology.boundary: Permissions to view flows still apply.

terminology.plain: A number from 1 to 2,000 that sequences same-object before-save or after-save flows.
terminology.precise: Assign a trigger order so flows run in a predictable sequence, for example by team or logical owner.
terminology.non_example: Approval process step order is a different product.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex trigger order is APEX-009, not this Flow value.
terminology.boundary: Values outside 1–2000 are not documented here.

terminology.plain: A time-offset path on a record-triggered Flow, not before-save.
terminology.precise: Help: run part of the flow at a configurable offset after the triggering event, such as a follow-up three days later.
terminology.example: Email three days after LAB_ Quote create.
terminology.non_example: Before-save field default is not a scheduled path.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Schedule-triggered Flow: a different type that runs on a clock for a batch (AUTO-005).
terminology.boundary: Do not quote unofficial async governor numbers.

terminology.plain: The triggering record in a record-triggered or schedule-triggered interview.
terminology.precise: Triggered Flows notes $Record for schedule-triggered interviews; record-triggered flows also work with the triggering record in the Start element.
terminology.non_example: A formula field on the object is not $Record.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: recordId in a screen Flow: a different input contract (AUTO-002).
terminology.boundary: Working with the triggering record has its own Help article; this lesson is the before/after fork.

when_to_use: Use before-save record-triggered Flow when you only need to update fields on the triggering record before it is saved, not when a validation rule must refuse illegal data.
Use after-save record-triggered Flow when you need actions and related records—Tasks, emails, Get Records—after the save commits.
Use a validation rule instead of any record-triggered Flow when the formula is True because the value is invalid and must never save.
Use a formula field when the value should calculate without a Flow interview, and an approval process when a person must decide.
Use Apex or Batch Apex only when Help's complementary cases apply; do not write Apex for a same-record stamp before-save Flow can do.
when_not_to_use: Do not use before-save Flow to send email, create related records, or collect a manager approval—that is after-save, approval, or another tool.
Do not use after-save Flow as a substitute for a validation rule that must block the save.
Do not use a formula field or validation rule when the need is a related Task after Closed Won—that is after-save Flow.
Do not use Apex as the default for fast field updates on the same record.
Do not use a scheduled path when you meant before-save; scheduled paths are time offsets after the event.

interview_questions.question: Before-save versus after-save record-triggered Flow?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Before-save updates the same record before the database save and is documented as faster than a record-change process. After-save is actions and related records after the save.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at the outcome. Same-record fields: Fast Field Updates. Tasks, email, Get Records: Actions and Related Records. I mention Flow Trigger Explorer and trigger order 1–2000 when multiple flows exist. I keep validation for illegal saves and Apex for complementary CPU or Batch cases.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Status default before-save; waitlist plus email after-save.
follow_ups: Where is order of execution documented?

interview_questions.question: Why not a validation rule for a Status default?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Validation True means invalid and blocks save. A default is a field update on a legal record—that is before-save Flow, not validation.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If Status blank is allowed and we want Enrolled, that is a stamp, not a refusal. If Status blank must never save, that is validation. Interviewers mix the two. A formula field cannot always write a user-editable default the same way a before-save Assignment can.
interview_questions.example: Blank LAB_ Status becomes Enrolled on insert via before-save.
follow_ups: Does before-save run on Data Loader?

interview_questions.question: Your before-save Flow never sends the welcome email. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Before-save is fast field updates on the triggering record. Communication is an after-save action. Move Send Email to an Actions and Related Records flow.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the Start element. If it is Fast Field Updates, email does not belong there. I do not rewrite in Apex for an email Help lists as Flow communication. I also check entry conditions and deliverability only after the path is after-save.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Contact before-save that attempted Send Email.
follow_ups: Could a scheduled path send it later?
Would a screen Flow be better?

interview_questions.question: Two before-save flows overwrite Discount__c. What do you do?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Open Flow Trigger Explorer, then assign trigger order values between 1 and 2,000 so they run in a known sequence—or combine the logic if one owner should own the field.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not guess that last-modified metadata wins. I do not jump to Apex. I check whether a formula field or validation should own the number instead of two Flows fighting.
interview_questions.example: Sales order 10 then Finance order 20 both assigning LAB_ Discount__c.
follow_ups: Does after-save also use trigger order?
How do async paths show in Explorer?
weak_answer_warnings: Deleting one flow without talking to the owner

interview_questions.question: When would you still write Apex instead of record-triggered Flow?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the work is CPU-intensive or the volume exceeds what scheduled-triggered Flow can handle—Help's complementary table—not for a same-record stamp.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I still pick before-save Flow for fast field updates and after-save for related Tasks. I may call invocable Apex from after-save if one step is code. I will not quote unofficial governor numbers in this lesson.
interview_questions.example: Complex discount engine vs defaulting LAB_ Type__c.

interview_questions.question: What does Flow Trigger Explorer add that Setup → Flows does not?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: It filters to one object and trigger type and shows before-save, after-save, and asynchronous paths together so you can navigate and reorder.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use it in interviews to prove I can find collisions. Setup's full flow list mixes screen and autolaunched types. Explorer is the record-triggered map. It does not replace validation, formula, or approval lists.
interview_questions.example: Opportunity Explorer listing two before-save and one after-save LAB_ flow.
follow_ups: Can you open Builder from Explorer?

interview_questions.question: Related waitlist never updates though Status on the attendee changes.

interview_questions.question: Airport analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Before-save is passport control on the same passport; after-save is the arrivals concierge creating tickets and sending texts. It breaks because one Salesforce save also runs validation, Apex triggers, and maybe scheduled paths—more rooms than two.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add that the 10x claim is versus a record-change process, not Apex. Formula is the printed visa class; approval is a human interview; validation is refused entry. I never use a labeled-drawer story.
